primaryStudies.citation: Synthesis and characterization of the N-terminal acetylated 17-23 fragment of thymosin beta 4 identified in TB-500, a product suspected to possess doping potential.
primaryStudies.keyFindings: Ac-LKKTETQ identified in the tested TB-500 material; analytical identity does not demonstrate efficacy.
primaryStudies.verificationScope: Abstract and bibliographic record; full-text audit incomplete

primaryStudies.citation: Doping control analysis of TB-500, a synthetic version of an active region of thymosin β₄, in equine urine and plasma by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry.
primaryStudies.studyType: fragment analytical detection with horse administration
primaryStudies.keyFindings: Ac-LKKTETQ and metabolites detected in equine samples after administration; analytical study, not a healing trial.
primaryStudies.verificationScope: Abstract and bibliographic record; full-text audit incomplete

primaryStudies.citation: Simultaneous quantification of TB-500 and its metabolites in in-vitro experiments and rats by UHPLC-Q-Exactive orbitrap MS/MS and their screening by wound healing activities in-vitro.
primaryStudies.keyFindings: Metabolism studied in laboratory human serum and rats; only Ac-LKKTE, not Ac-LKKTETQ, showed significant wound-healing assay activity.
primaryStudies.verificationScope: Abstract and bibliographic record; full-text audit incomplete

primaryStudies.citation: TB500/TB1000 and SGF1000: A scientific approach for a better understanding of misbranded and adulterated drugs.
primaryStudies.keyFindings: Tested TB500/TB1000 products were not consistently described by prior labels; cannot generalize composition to every product.
primaryStudies.verificationScope: Abstract and bibliographic record; full-text audit incomplete

evidenceSummary.humanEvidence: Human fragment administration not verified in this bounded review
evidenceSummary.preclinicalEvidence: One directly cited fragment metabolism/activity report; analytical reports listed separately
evidenceSummary.keyFinding: Only Ac-LKKTE showed significant wound-healing activity in the cited 2024 assay; Ac-LKKTETQ did not. Parent clinical evidence is not fragment efficacy.
evidenceSummary.regulatoryStatus: Dated FDA May 15, 2026 briefing describes evaluated forms as unapproved drug components; final-rule inventory not verified

metadata.scope: Native-fragment/product analytical subset, not a complete bibliography. Dossier separately cites parent and related-molecule context. Open-access count withheld: not assessed.
